property_summary: After calling XBornID by the owner, the owner's balance equals totalDistributed (not totalSupply).
After a successful transferFrom by a spender, the spender's allowance for the from-address strictly decreases by the transferred amount (i.e., allowance_after == allowance_before - amount).

If a spender successfully calls transferFrom to move tokens from an owner to another address, then immediately after the call the spender's allowance for that owner must be strictly less than or equal to the spender's balance (i.e., allowance does not momentarily observe the pre-transfer value while balances were updated).

After a successful transferFrom by spender, the spender's allowance for the owner is decreased (strictly) and any immediate visible allowance read after the call equals the previous allowance minus the transferred amount.

If transferFrom succeeds, then a concurrent reentrant view of allowance (via a callback during transferFrom) must observe the allowance after it has been decremented (i.e. the spender cannot observe the old allowance value during the transfer).

After a successful transferFrom call, the spender's allowance for the from-address is not observed (via the public allowance getter) to be greater than the post-transfer balance of the spender (i.e. allowance <= balanceOf(spender)).

For any caller, when transferFrom transfers _amount from _from to _to it always decreases allowed[_from][caller] by _amount (so allowed after the call equals previous allowed minus _amount); the mutant that reorders state updates can make allowed differ (observable via getter) after certain interleavings/reads, so there exists inputs where the mutant's allowed value does not equal the original's.

For any caller A, spender S, and amount v where S is approved by A for at least v and A has at least v balance, after calling transferFrom(A, T, v) the reference contract always decreases allowed[A][S] by exactly v (observable via allowance(A,S)); the mutant's reordered writes can be observed by a reentrant spender S that reads allowance mid-transfer and thus can make the final stored allowance differ, so the property fails for some inputs when S is a reentrant contract.

For every caller S, owner A and amount v where transferFrom(A,T,v) is allowed and A has sufficient balance, the reference contract always ends with allowance(A,S) decreased by exactly v (observable via allowance); the mutant's reordered updates can be observed by a reentrant spender S that calls allowance during transferFrom and causes final stored allowance to differ for some inputs.

For any spender S approved by owner A for amount v and with A having sufficient balance, calling transferFrom(A, T, v) never changes allowance(A,S) except by decreasing it by v in the reference contract; the mutant that moves the allowed decrement after balance updates can be distinguished because a reentrant spender can call back into the token during transferFrom and make the final stored allowance differ.

For any approved spender S, owner A and amount v where S has allowance>=v and A has balance>=v, calling transferFrom(A, T, v) on the reference always results in allowance(A,S) decreased by v (observable via allowance); the mutant that moves the allowed decrement after balances can be distinguished when S is a reentrant contract that calls allowance during transferFrom, producing a different final stored allowance for some inputs.
After transferFrom used by spender, the allowance stored for that spender decreases by the transferred amount.

After a successful transferFrom by an approved spender, subsequent transferFroms by the same spender cannot exceed the original allowance remaining (i.e., allowance is reduced by transfers), so a second transferFrom that together with the first would cumulatively exceed the initial allowance must revert or fail in the original but succeeds in the mutant.
After a successful transferFrom by a spender, the allowance returned by allowance(owner, spender) strictly decreases by the transferred amount.

property_summary: A successful transferFrom by a spender does not increase the reported allowance for that (owner, spender) pair (allowance_after <= allowance_before).
A successful transferFrom by spender reduces the remaining allowance such that a subsequent transferFrom of the same amount will revert (i.e., allowance enforces cumulative usage).
